messages.subject: Problem Running Report Survey
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to run the report survey function but I always obtained this error:

Error: Cannot read date format in CTtable[, setupCol]. Output is all NA. expected: %Y-%m-%D actual: 2021-01-28

I think apparently the format of my dates columns are not accurate. As I had to do some changes to the data, I had to apply some changes on these columns and change the format. Here is the code I run:
reportTest <- surveyReport (recordTable          = Record_Table_PLWS_GridA,
                            CTtable              = Camera_Deployment_PLWS_GridA,
                            speciesCol           = "Species",
                            stationCol           = "Station",
                            setupCol             = "Setup_date",
                            retrievalCol         = "Retrieval_date",
                            CTDateFormat         = "%Y-%m-%D",
                            recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                            recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                            CTHasProblems        = FALSE)

How do I change the format of the dates column for it to work ?

Thank you for your help,

Regards,

Emeline Auda

messages.subject: Re: Problem Running Report Survey
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emeline & David,
David is right, I didn't check carefully enough. See ?strptime:

%d
Day of the month as decimal number (01–31).

%D
Date format such as %m/%d/%y: the C99 standard says it should be that exact format (but not all OSes comply).

So it must be %d and not %D. Since all that strptime stuff can be quite confusing, I'd recommend the lubridate format.

David, with regard to Emeline's second question, I saw the email but don't know why it doesn't appear here on the group. I answered personally via email already.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Occasion length in Detection History
messages.body_plain: Hi, I'm looking for advice for determining which occasion length to choose for detection histories. I've played around a bit in unmarked and have found increasing the occasion length increases species detectability. My species is one that has high occupancy (~0.9) and low detectability (~0.1 to 0.2), but I am unsure on what the best occasion length to choose is (i.e. 1-day, 3-day, 6-day etc.). Any suggestions on this would be great!
messages.body_snippet: Hi, I'm looking for advice for determining which occasion length to choose for detection histories. I've played around a bit in unmarked and have found increasing the occasion length increases species

messages.subject: Re: Occasion length in Detection History
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tim,
there are no fixed rules, and it's hard to say in general. Normally, when you change the occasion length, only the detection probabilities should change. Relationships between occupancy and site covariates should remain (almost) the same when varying occasion length. Hence, if you are interested in ecological relationships with site covariates, it doesn't matter much, and also shouldn't affect results much. Just make sure the models converge and give reasonable estimates, and occupancy estimates remain constant.

Nevertheless, you don't want to use too short occasions, otherwise the detection probabilities are very low which might lead to problems in parameter estimation.
You don't want to go too high either, since you need at least two occasions (better more) to estimate detection probability.

Longer occasions also tend to collapse multiple detections into single events, thus losing information. Since your species is common, it's not a big problem, and instead more of a consideration for rare species where every record counts.
That being said,  you can check how many "1"s there are in your detection history, and think about how many records you are willing to sacrifice by using longer occasions. The whole question comes down to a trade-off between preserving records and ensuring adequate detection probabilities.

If you are in doubt you can also present some results in the unmarked Google group  <https://groups.google.com/g/unmarked>or the hierarchical modelling in ecology group <https://groups.google.com/g/hmecology> and ask advice there, both groups are more suited for modelling questions.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Formatting warnings - recordTable and dectionHistory. And a bug?
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Formatting warnings - recordTable and dectionHistory. And a bug?
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

I agree, the console output is messy. Can you please reinstall from github and see if the warnings are better now?

About the possible bug, what version of camtrapR are you using? I'd need to check more carefully with the actual data. Feel free to privately email me a workspace with a little subset of the data, just enough to reproduce the error. I'll have a look then.

Also, please share the function call of detectionHistory. Did you set any other arguments that may potentially affect the survey duration (e.g. maxNumberDays)?

Normally, detectionHistory should of course include records on the retrieval day. In the current CRAN release, it should the 23:59:59 on the retrieval day, as you said. In v2.1 (on github), the user can optionally set the time of camera retrieval (in the camera table that is used by cameraOperation). If it is not provided, the function will assume 12 noon for retrieval (same for setup by the way), so records after noon would be excluded if retrieval time is not defined. But telling from the time of the records that's not the case here since the records are from the morning.

I'll have a closer look if you send me the data.

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Help with Independent Records
messages.body_plain:
Hello Marion,

don't worry, you came to the right place. And you already found out that this is done via camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence.

But first of all your table seems to contain both records and the camera trap information. This is redundant, since the coordiantes and dates will the identical for all records at the same stations. So the first thing I'd suggest is make two separate tables, one for the camera trap stations and one for the records. See ?camtraps and ?recordTableSample, or the vignettes of camtrapR.

Then, how do you want to take the number of animals into account? What would you like to do with that information when extracting independent events?

TO get the DateTimeOriginal column, it might be easiest to use

library(lubridate)

and then create a new date/time column with:

base$DateTimeOriginal <- dmy_HMS(paste(base$Photo.Date, base$Photo.Time))

I haven't tested this though.

Best regards,

Jürgen

Hi Angela & Lucero,

The problem is the double forward slash you can see in the error message.

Change it to
NHead_test <- ("H:/PhD/Camera footage/Tunnels/NorthHead")

Additional subdirectories should not cause problems.

Jürgen
